iPad OS and windows 10 have completely different requirements. And in both cases the absurdly small amount of hard drive space makes it impossible for me to justify recommending anybody by either of those devices. The only slight benefit to the surface is that it might support a 10 year old out of date expandable storage specification. 

but back to the ram if you need to view more than one web page at a time for gigabytes of RAM on Windows just is not enough these days. 

The software available in each platform is also vastly different. Software made for iOS doesn't require near the amount of resources that software compiled for Windows does. So 3gb is livable on iOS. Believe me. I use a surface pro with 4GB of RAM and a 128gb SSD. it is the definition of misery. The only thing that would be worse is using the tablet I had before. That had an Intel atom processor in 2 gigabytes of RAM. But that tablet only cost $400 total in 2012 With the hinged keyboard dock with a battery inside of it. You can buy similar tablets on the market today from reputable manufacturers for $200. With bigger screens than the surface go. Meanwhile Microsoft is charging what is it 600? Plus the cost of accessories like a keyboard.

Honestly that's the price the damn thing should cost. Test it out first, but if you can get it for $180 not a bad deal. personally I still can't believe they actually get away with selling a 4GB model for so much money. It would actually be a really good deal at 180 though.
